renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: hrd_probability_gauge
  title: HRD probability
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest probability of homologous recombination deficiency over the tumors in view, shown against the cut-off CHORD uses to call a tumor deficient. It answers whether any tumor is called HR deficient.
    How to read: a value below the cut-off is called HR proficient and a value at or above it HR deficient. A call can still be undetermined when the tumor has too few indels or SVs, so check the table remarks.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is a probability of 0.5, the value at which CHORD calls a sample HR deficient. The probability is the sum of the BRCA1-type and BRCA2-type probabilities, as CHORD's code computes it.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/chord/README.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UMCUGenetics/CHORD/master/R/chordPredict.R
  column: p_hrd
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - min
  - median
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.5
  threshold_direction: max
  caption: against the 0.5 HRD cut-off
  headline: true

- component: table
  id: hrd_table
  title: HRD prediction table
  description: |-
    Each row is a tumor with its BRCA1-type, BRCA2-type and overall HRD probabilities, the HR status call, the HRD subtype and the remarks that explain an undetermined call. It answers which tumors are deficient and of which type.
    How to read: the status is deficient when the HRD probability is at least 0.5. CHORD needs at least 100 indels to call the status and at least 30 SVs to call the subtype, and it cannot be applied to MSI tumors, so read the remarks before trusting a call.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/chord/README.md
